sections.body: COOKING: learn 5 cheap, healthy meals (rice and lentils, pasta with vegetables, eggs, stir-fry, soup). Batch-cook to save money and time.
LAUNDRY: check labels, separate darks and lights, and don't overload the machine.
RENTING: read the whole contract before signing, photograph the place when you move in, know the deposit rules, and never send money for a place you haven't seen (a common scam).
TRAVEL SAFETY: share your plans with someone, keep copies of documents, use licensed transport, and keep emergency numbers saved.

quiz.q: Why photograph a rented flat when you move in?
options: To prove its condition so you get your deposit back
It's required to unlock the door
hints: What happens when you move out?
If you borrowed a car with a scratch already on it, a photo proves you didn't cause it.
quiz.explain: Photos record the original condition, protecting your deposit.

quiz.q: An online advert for a cheap flat asks for a deposit before you can view it. This is likely…
hints: Would you pay for something you can't see?
Rental scams often ask for money up front.
If someone sold concert tickets but refused to show proof they exist, would you pay?
quiz.explain: Paying before viewing is a classic rental scam warning sign.

quiz.q: A white shirt washed with a new pair of dark jeans comes out blue-grey. Which laundry tip would have prevented this?
hints: Where did the colour on the shirt come from?
New, dark fabrics can release dye in the wash, and other clothes can absorb it.
Worked example: a wool jumper that shrank in a hot wash would have been saved by checking its care label first. Here the problem is different: colour moved from one item to another.
quiz.explain: New, dark items (especially denim) can release dye in the wash. Washing darks and lights separately stops lighter clothes picking up that colour.
